source_text: Ἐν αὐτῇ δὲ ταύτῃ (epistola) καὶ τῆς Κλήμεντος πρὸς Κορινθίους μέμνηται ἐπιστολῆς, (verba Eusebii sunt in loco modo signato) δηλῶν ἀνέκαθεν ἐξ ἀρχαίου ἔθους ἐπὶ τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὴν ἀνάγνωσιν αὐτῆς ποιεῖσθαι. λέγει γοῦν (Dionysius) Τὴν σήμερον οὖν Κυριακὴν ἁγίαν ἡμέραν διηγάγομεν, ἐν ᾗ ἀνέγνωμεν ὑμῶν τὴν ἐπιστολήν· ἣν ἕξομεν ἀεί ποτε ἀναγινώσκοντες νουθετεῖσθαι, ὡς καὶ τὴν προτέραν ἡμῖν διὰ Κλήμεντος γραφεῖσαν.
thought_title: Public reading of the Roman and Clementine letters on the Lord's day
orientation: Dionysius is writing to the Roman church, recalling how he and his church read the Romans' letter on the Lord's day and will keep reading it for admonition, just as they do the earlier letter written through Clement.
pass_a_gloss: And in this same letter he also mentions the letter of Clement to the Corinthians, making clear that from the beginning, from ancient custom, the reading of it is done in the church. He says at any rate: The holy Lord's day today then we spent, on which we read your letter; which we will always have, reading it, to be admonished, as also the former one written to us through Clement.

choices.why: Keeps the adjective order and the liturgical sense of the day of worship; 'holy' is retained because it is in the source.
rejected: the holy day of the Lord

choices.why: The verb means to pass or spend time; 'spent' preserves the imperfect sense of an ongoing observance.
The passive infinitive expresses the purpose of the reading; 'admonished' keeps the corrective, pastoral force.

choices.english: from the beginning, from ancient custom
choices.why: Both temporal phrases are kept in source order to show the doubled emphasis on long-standing practice.
rejected: from ancient custom from the beginning
from the start by ancient custom

choices.why: The preposition with the genitive indicates the setting where the reading is done; 'in the church' is the plainest literal rendering.

pass_b_english: In this same letter he also mentions Clement's letter to the Corinthians, making clear that from the beginning, from ancient custom, its reading was done in the church. Dionysius says: "Today we spent the holy Lord's day, and on it we read your letter. We will always have it to read for our admonition, just as we do the former one written to us through Clement."

problems.quote: In this same letter he also mentions Clement's letter
problems.why: 'He' is ambiguous—Eusebius narrating about Dionysius, or someone else?
problems.fix: Clarify that Eusebius is narrating about Dionysius's letter.

edits.old: In this same letter he also mentions Clement's letter
edits.new: In this same letter Dionysius also mentions Clement's letter

fixed: Clarified 'he' to 'Dionysius' since Eusebius is narrating about Dionysius's letter, and the pronoun was ambiguous.
